candidate_relations.reason: Both are disseminated infections in an immunocompromised (HIV) host with pulmonary and CNS involvement, making TB a plausible differential. However, the reference diagnosis specifies Rhodococcus equi as the causative organism — a distinct bacterial pathogen classically associated with HIV, cat/animal exposure, necrotizing/cavitary pneumonia, and brain abscess. TB is a competing diagnosis with an incompatible etiology and somewhat different anatomical pattern (necrotizing/liquefactive lung lesion with ring-enhancing brain abscesses are more characteristic of Rhodococcus equi than typical TB). The candidate asserts a different causative organism and thus conflicts with the required specificity of the reference.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Disseminated TB with CNS involvement vs. Rhodococcus equi causing necrotizing pneumonia, bacteremia, and brain abscess in HIV-positive patient

case_quality_flags: Cat exposure and homosexuality (HIV risk factor) are classic epidemiological clues for Rhodococcus equi, distinguishing it from TB
Necrotizing/liquefactive lung lesion on CT and ring-enhancing brain abscesses are more consistent with Rhodococcus equi than disseminated TB
HIV status not explicitly confirmed by laboratory testing in the record, though strongly implied by clinical context
